reuse.why: Consumers reuse the shared weekend helpers, but getUpcomingDates repeats the daily-skip predicate and the range handler independently derives adjustment bounds.

duplication.why: Daily-skip eligibility and holiday-dependent adjustment bounds each have multiple definitions.

placement.why: Holiday recognition and date adjustment belong in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handler also owns knowledge about the adjustment policy.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on the requested scheduling changes, their consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The split skip-and-adjust interface, independently maintained traversal bounds, and untyped handler config make future scheduling changes harder to maintain consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates reimplements shared/schedules.ts:dropsWeekends with rule.skipWeekend && rule.frequency === 'daily'.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange expresses adjustment reach as 3 + holidays.length while applyWeekendRule expresses it as 2 + holidays.length, reshaping the same policy knowledge into a separate range-padding calculation.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays; applyWeekendRule adds daily-frequency handling and an invalid-mode fallback, while getUpcomingDates independently repeats the daily-skip dispatch.
